answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each identity to lock a refundable stake that decays slowly, like an ember that must be tended: new identities earn trust only through sustained honest work, and misbehavior burns the stake. A raven that copies itself into a flock still pays full price for every bird, so flooding the network costs more than it gains. Reputation is recorded in a public sonnet of attestations, a ledger peers can audit, so cheap identities stay visibly untrusted while proven ones accumulate weight.
